## Decision: SHIP — variant_c

## Primary result
Conversion (primary, higher is better): **variant_c vs control: +9.41% (95% CI +2.21% to +17.1%), p = 0.0096; absolute +0.009016 (0.09585 -> 0.1049); better** [r3]. With Holm correction across the three treatment arms, variant_c remains significant: **adjusted p = 0.029** [r5]. variant_b and variant_d are inconclusive (adjusted p = 0.66 each) [r5].

## Guardrails
Bounce guardrail (higher is worse): **variant_c vs control: -2.25% (95% CI -5.59% to +1.21%), p = 0.2; guardrail passed (no statistically significant harm)** [r4]. variant_b and variant_d also passed the bounce guardrail [r4].

## Validity checks (SRM, peeking, novelty)
- **SRM passed**: observed split control 24.95% / variant_b 25.13% / variant_c 24.68% / variant_d 25.24%; chi2 = 4.188, p = 0.24 [r2].
- **Peeking**: no planned interim looks, so no sequential test was required [r1].
- **Novelty**: daily data is not available for this experiment, so a daily-effects decay check could not be run [r1].

## Caveats
- The observed primary effect (+9.41% relative) is just below the pre-registered MDE of 10% relative, although the confidence interval excludes zero [r1][r3].
- Revenue is listed as a secondary metric in the plan but was not part of the ship decision rule and was not analyzed here [r1].
- No daily data, so a novelty/decay check could not be performed [r1].

## Exploratory findings
None run; not needed for the decision.
